From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary dedicated lane request for NovaMed POC

Hi team,

Quick ask: NovaMed (Sarah Lee) is launching a short clinical inference pilot starting Apr 12–23 and needs a predictable, low-latency dedicated lane for inference. Sales flagged this as time-sensitive because they have an external demo with their clinical partners on Apr 19. Details below: 

- Pilot window: Apr 12 00:00 UTC – Apr 23 23:59 UTC (11 days active runtime)
- Capacity requested: equivalent of 4x A100-class GPUs (sustained), single-region (us-west), with an autoscale exception so the pool does not scale-to-zero during the window
- Expected TTI: median tail latency target 120ms for 512-token prompts; throughput ~120 reqs/sec
- Data flow: encrypted uploads via our hosted API; no PHI stored long term (customer asserts ephemeral processing) — we still need to confirm retention policy for the logs

Attachments: pilot map and initial SLA addendum (attached). Please review capacity feasibility and ops constraints. Two asks for ops/product for Monday: 

1) Ops: Can we provision a temporary dedicated slate (reserve) that guarantees the requested headroom with a temporary autoscale policy (no scale-to-zero, allow short burst overcommit) for Apr 12–23? What's the cost estimate and the operational risk?
2) Product/Legal: We need a stopgap SLA addendum that covers the pilot window and clarifies responsibility for retention/audit logs. I attached a first pass (draft-sla-addendum-REV1.pdf).

If this needs an executive sign-off path, flag it — sales is pushing a demo date and would like a yes/no by EOD Friday.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- 20270329-novamed-pilot-map.xlsx (spreadsheet: pilot schedule & traffic profile)
- draft-sla-addendum-REV1.pdf (PDF: temporary SLA language)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Mar 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary dedicated lane request for NovaMed POC

Laura — thanks for the clear breakdown. I ran this past the allocation planner and ops constraints that matter for this ask: 

- Short answer: provisioning is plausible, but we need to formalize an autoscale exception and a prebooked buffer so the cluster scheduler won't evict these nodes for normal reclaim. That requires a temporary reservation ticket and a manual override on the autoscaler for the window.

- Operational constraints/notes:
  * We can provide an equivalent of 4x A100 capacity by carving a transient slate from the us-west pool. That will reduce headroom for other live pilots that week — Marcus, please confirm whether any other committed pilots consume overlapping capacity Apr 12–23.
  * Autoscale exception: we can set a no-scale-to-zero policy for the reservation, but we need to cap burst overcommit to +25% and maintain preemptible fallback to a quantized model variant if we hit >90% utilization for >10 minutes.
  * Runbook: we'll need an on-call routing plan and a short rollback playbook if latency degrades. I can sketch the runbook, but it requires Marcus and Aditya to sign off on the monitoring thresholds.

- Cost: rough estimate for a 11-day carve (4x A100 equivalent) is ~$36k — this includes dedicated runtime and a 20% ops surcharge for manual override. I'll confirm exact numbers after Marcus verifies overlapping commitments.

Action items for this thread:
1) Marcus: confirm other commitments in us-west Apr 12–23 and whether the CARVE is permissible.
2) Aditya: coordinate the billing/quote addendum for the customer and confirm whether Sales is comfortable with the ops surcharge.
3) Laura/Product: confirm acceptance of the +25% burst cap and fallback to quant model; Legal to review attached SLA addendum for any data-retention clauses we must change.

Also attaching a small capacity note I used in a previous carve (capacity-runbook-stub.pdf) — will adapt for NovaMed once we have sign-offs.

—Kimberly
Head of Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the assessment, Kimberly — this approach sounds fine with two caveats:

1) Keep the burst cap conservative (+25% seems reasonable). If we need temporary additional headroom beyond that, the escalation path must be to Product/Sales to accept degraded SLAs for non-demo traffic, not Ops unilaterally increasing carve.
2) Legal: please prioritize a one-paragraph retention/audit line in the SLA addendum that explicitly states logs will be ephemeral and retention limited to 72 hours for pilot telemetry. If Legal can't confirm immediately, we can gate the pilot on an internal audit waiver.

Please treat this as a green light to proceed with a temporary carve for Apr 12–23 provided Marcus confirms no conflicting commitments (Marcus: can you confirm by EOD today?). Laura/Aditya: if Sales needs the customer quote, have Aditya produce a one-off quote with the ops surcharge and tag it to deal RWF-4721.

I'll be copied on the final mutual action plan but otherwise consider this approved from Product.

—Karthik
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
